analysis.title: The tech sector's rout spoils the party
key_insights: After the Democrats' landslide in the US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell 5% in its worst day in five months, putting it more than 10% below its 6 October record high and reviving doubts about AI sector momentum.
The trigger is political, not macroeconomic: Democratic control of Congress has cast doubt on the viability of many data centre construction projects, particularly in Texas.
Brent crude fell nearly 9% on Wednesday to 94 $/bbl, then rebounded 3.1% to 98 $/bbl on Thursday. A Democratic Congress constrains the Trump administration's military options regarding Iran.
Flows through the Strait of Hormuz are returning to normal (17.1 mb/d exported from the Gulf in October) and Qatar is stepping up its mediation efforts.

The BoE raised Bank Rate by 25bp to 4.00%, its first hike since August 2023, in an 8-1 vote (Mann wanted 50bp). Communication rules out a prolonged series of hikes for now but warns this is unlikely to be the last unless the Middle East conflict is resolved.
The 2y Gilt yield rose 5bp to 4.79% and the market prices nearly three more BoE hikes by end-2027. The BoE expects CPI inflation to peak at 4.9% in Q2 2027.
US 2y Treasury yields rose 12bp to 4.46% and the 2s10s spread steepened 7bp to 37bp. The 10y Bund yield fell 3bp to 3.24%, and the OAT-Bund spread widened 4bp to 154bp.

In US equities the NDX fell more than 6%, the SOX fell 12%, the Magnificent 7 fell 4% and Tesla fell 10% on fears that Congress might restrict AI development. The VIX rose to 28 and all SPX sectors closed lower.
European equities closed with moderate losses (SX5E -0.5%), with tech down 4% and retail up 1.7%.

Tech credit widened in the afternoon: Oracle 5-year CDS moved back above 300bp (+14bp), SpaceX 5-year CDS rose 21bp to 297bp, and cash spreads on Oracle, Nvidia and SpaceX widened an average of 10, 5 and 10bp.

European defence stocks fell broadly after Rheinmetall cut its full-year revenue guidance for the second time (frigate contract cancelled, Boxer orders pushed to 2027). Rheinmetall shares fell 17%, RENK fell 6.3%, and the US midterm results added pressure.
Leonardo beat Q3 expectations on EBITA and order intake and raised order guidance for the second time this year. Hensoldt raised its 2026 guidance, with order intake up 77% over nine months.
CMZB Q3 26: revenue slightly missed, the bottom line beat, and net profit rose 45% YoY to €859mn. FY26 NII guidance was trimmed on deposit competition, and the focus is on the UniCredit takeover.
The US October employment report is due tomorrow, with consensus expecting a recovery in job creation.
French mortgage rates reached 3.49% in October from 3.40% in September, and mortgage lending fell 4.2% YoY.

market_movers.rationale: Tesla fell 10%, leading the Magnificent 7 lower, on fears that the Democratic-controlled Congress might restrict AI development.
Nvidia dollar cash spreads widened about 5bp as tech credit sold off on AI and data-centre slowdown fears.
Oracle 5-year CDS moved back above 300bp (+14bp) and cash spreads widened about 10bp on AI and data-centre concerns.
Rheinmetall shares fell 17% after a second cut to full-year revenue guidance, dragging the European defence sector.
Leonardo beat Q3 EBITA and order intake expectations and raised order guidance, but the shares were weighed down by the sector decline.

sector_views.rationale: Rotation away from semiconductors and AI continued, with the SOX down 12% and tech credit spreads widening on political risk to data-centre buildout.
Sector-wide decline after Rheinmetall's guidance cut, German contract cancellations and postponements, and uncertainty over US defence spending after the midterms.

earnings_insights: Commerzbank (CMZB) Q3 26 reported: slight revenue miss against expectations, bottom-line beat, costs in line, cost of risk marginally better than expected. Revenue up 9% YoY, net profit up 45% YoY to €859mn. FY26 NII guidance modestly trimmed, FY revenue and earnings targets reiterated.
Leonardo Q3 reported: EBITA and order intake significantly beat expectations, revenue slightly above. Full-year order guidance raised for the second time this year.
RENK reported: order intake +33.6% to €1.66bn, backlog €7.59bn, revenue +5.8%, adjusted net income down. Shares down 6.3%.
Rheinmetall 9M reported: revenue +38% to €8.38bn, EBIT +68% to €1.34bn, backlog €78bn. Full-year revenue guidance cut for the second time. Shares down 17%.
Hensoldt 9M reported: order intake +77%, backlog +46% to €10.37bn, revenue +18%, adjusted EBITDA +33%, free cash flow negative. 2026 guidance raised.
Engie 9M-26 reported in line: EBIT excluding nuclear €7.0bn, up 10% YoY reported and 3% organic. 2026 guidance raised, with recurring net income now expected at the upper end of the €4.9-5.5bn range.
Veolia 9M-26 reported in line: EBITDA €5.40bn, up 5% organic. 2026 targets confirmed.

Orsted 9M-26 reported: recurring EBITDA DKK20.2bn, up 19% YoY. Q3 impairments of DKK3.4bn on higher long-term US rates. Recurring EBITDA guidance of >DKK28bn confirmed and 2026 gross investment guidance cut 10% to DKK45-50bn.
EDP 9M-26 reported: recurring EBITDA €4.17bn, up 11% YoY. Net debt €16.8bn at 30/09/26.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A 25bp hike, the first since August 2023, with a path of further hikes priced by the market.
The BoE expects inflation to peak at 4.9% in Q2 2027, supporting the hawkish tone.
Brent fell nearly 9% to 94 $/bbl on Wednesday, then rebounded 3.1% to 98 $/bbl on Thursday, as the midterm result constrains US military options on Iran.
Flows through the Strait of Hormuz are returning to normal.

macro_indicators.reading: Consensus expects a recovery in job creation
macro_indicators.interpretation: The release is due tomorrow at 14:30 CET and is the next key event after the equity rout.
Up from 3.40% in September, pushing first-time buyers out of the market.

risk_factors: Political risk to AI and data-centre buildout from Democratic control of Congress, particularly projects in Texas.
Escalation in the Middle East, since the BoE warns further hikes are likely unless the conflict is resolved.
Possible Iranian emboldening after the US election result.
German government contract cancellations and postponements, and uncertainty over US defence spending.
Widening tech credit spreads and CDS, with Oracle and SpaceX 5-year CDS near or above 300bp.
vol_and_positioning: The VIX rose to 28 after the equity sell-off, and VIX futures closed at 23.9 (+6.8 points).
The rotation away from semiconductors and AI continued, with the SOX down 12% and the NDX down more than 6%.
The market expects nearly three further BoE rate rises by end-2027.
geopolitical: Democratic landslide in the US midterms, with control of Congress constraining the Trump administration's military options regarding Iran.
Strait of Hormuz flows returning to normal, with 17.1 mb/d exported from the Gulf in October, and Qatar stepping up mediation efforts.

French National Assembly unanimously rejected the revenue section of the state budget (458 votes against, none in favour), and the budget goes to the Senate in its original version, with discussions starting November 20.
Rheinmetall frigate contract cancelled and Boxer orders postponed to 2027, raising concerns about German government commitments.

tension_points.bull_case: Commerzbank-style earnings and defence order books show resilient fundamentals elsewhere, and the post-election relief rally suggests markets can recover quickly.
